_comment: Adding a row is a ruling routed to @system_adamic, and only Adamic adds one. Each row is one fixture whose backends are ruled to differ, from each other, or, where node is set, both from the source on Node while they agree with each other; name is the ruled divergence, which may hold more than one fixture. Schema: divergences lists fixture (the program's repository path, once), name (absent for a lone row), ruling (who ruled, naming the task; a row whose ruling is empty or names no task is refused), reason, format (absent for a program built as an ES module; CommonJSBundle for one built only as one bundled image, which the installed-layout harness runs with each leg's lib directory written <lib>), node (absent where Node's side isn't ruled), native and javascript, each outcome its exact stdout, stderr and exit_code. internal/oracle's backend divergence test holds each fixture's runs to its row byte for byte, and the admission delta reads a program at a row's fixture as that divergence only when Node's and native's runs are exactly the row's and native and JavaScript agree, or, for a row a test holds apart on purpose, JavaScript's run is exactly the row's too. An outcome's {root} is the admission delta's checkout, for a stop that names its program's file; no fixture of the oracle's has one. Membership never excuses any other output.
